title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is part of the 1966 letter to Tate on crystals, §2.7–2.8. Earlier sections ask whether the de Rham invariant G(A) = (H^1_DR(A), Hodge filtration) of an abelian scheme A/S is 'rigid', i.e. independent of the chosen infinitesimal lifting. In char 0 this holds: an integrable connection there is the same thing as a stratification (descent data on all infinitesimal neighbourhoods P^n of the diagonal), and Gauss–Manin provides one. The previous page conjectures that over an Artinian base with residue field of char p, rigidity holds exactly for ordinary A. That is a Serre–Tate-type statement about canonical lifts and the Dieudonné filtration.

(1) Struck-out paragraph: an attempted proof that the conjecture fails over a positive-dimensional base.
- Take a modular scheme with level structure ('à échelons') for elliptic curves and localize at Z_p. This gives S smooth over Z_p, of relative dimension 1, carrying the rank-2 bundle H^1_DR(A/S).
- If rigidity held at ordinary points, then on S minus the finitely many supersingular closed points (Hasse invariant zero) one would get a stratification relative to Z_p.
- By purity (S is regular of dimension 2 and we remove codimension-2 points, so isomorphisms between locally free sheaves on each P^n extend), this stratification extends over all of S.
- Hence H^1_DR of the modular family in char p would carry a stratification. It would be Frobenius-compatible, since it is so off the supersingular points, contradicting 2.7.
- He crossed this out. The same argument is redone more carefully on the next page, phrased via crystals and gluing with the p-adic completion.

(2) Fallback. Perhaps in pure char p the rigidity statement for everywhere-ordinary A is still true. Then the ordinary locus would carry a canonical stratification on H^1_DR that does not extend over the whole modular curve, and the char-p and char-0 stratifications would refuse to glue. He calls this 'canularesque'.

(3) Bracketed meta-remark: stratification is an 'infinite' notion, unlike connection; char 0 hides this, since there the two coincide.
- Example: on H^1_DR of the modular family of elliptic schemes over Z, the generic fibre S_Q carries the natural stratification (Gauss–Manin).
- 'Almost' shown: it extends to a stratification over S_U for no nonempty open U ⊂ Spec Z. The 'almost' hinges on whether the char-p stratification would be Frobenius-respected, a point he says must be cleared up.
- He finds this 'moral': a module with stratification should play the role of an ℓ-adic sheaf and share its rigidity properties.

Modern reading. A stratification over S_U restricts mod p (p in U) to a connection with zero p-curvature. Katz (1970/72) showed that the p-curvature of Gauss–Manin on H^1_DR is computed by the Kodaira–Spencer map. For the modular family Kodaira–Spencer is an isomorphism, so the p-curvature is nonzero (nilpotent) for every p. Hence no extension exists for any U, and no Frobenius argument is needed. The same fact kills the hoped-for canonical stratification on the ordinary locus in char p, at least if its connection is required to be Gauss–Manin. That is the 'faux, n'est jamais vrai en car p>0!' of the later margin note on the previous page.
errors: The fallback hope (para 2) of a canonical stratification on H^1_DR over the ordinary locus in char p cannot hold if the associated connection is Gauss–Manin. GM has nonzero p-curvature there, by Katz's p-curvature = Kodaira–Spencer formula and the KS isomorphism, whereas a stratification forces p-curvature 0. Grothendieck's own later margin note on the previous page ('faux, n'est jamais vrai en car p>0 !') acknowledges the falsity.

The 'presque' (dependence on Frobenius compatibility) is unnecessary: the p-curvature obstruction alone shows the char-0 stratification extends over no S_U. This is a gap in the argument as written, not a false conclusion.

Struck paragraph: the purity step is fine (rank-2 bundle on a regular 2-dimensional scheme, finitely many closed points removed). The real flaw is the premise that rigidity holds at ordinary points of a positive-dimensional base.

ideas.what: Stratification on a module as an 'infinite' structure (data on all infinitesimal neighbourhoods), coinciding with an integrable connection only in char 0
ideas.modern_name: stratified modules / D-modules with full ring of differential operators; F-divided bundles (Katz–Gieseker)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology, 1966/68), Berthelot; Gieseker 1975
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin on H^1_DR of the universal elliptic curve over Q does not extend to a stratification over S_U for any nonempty open U ⊂ Spec Z
ideas.modern_name: nonvanishing of p-curvature of GM (Katz's p-curvature/Kodaira–Spencer formula); arithmetic side of the p-curvature conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz 1970/1972 (p-curvature of GM; Grothendieck–Katz conjecture stated by Katz, attributed to Grothendieck)
ideas.where_published: Conjecture recorded by Katz (Invent. Math. 1972); not in Grothendieck's own published texts to my knowledge

ideas.what: A stratified module should play the role of an ℓ-adic sheaf and share its rigidity
ideas.modern_name: stratified bundles as analogue of étale local systems; Gieseker's conjecture (Esnault–Mehta 2010)

ideas.what: Conjectural rigidity of the Dieudonné/de Rham invariant for ordinary abelian varieties over Artinian bases; canonical lifts
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate theory of ordinary abelian varieties, canonical coordinates

ideas.what: Purity extension of a stratification over finitely many removed closed points of a regular 2-dim scheme

missed.claim: An early (1966) formulation of the question behind the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture: when does a char-0 integrable connection (here GM on the modular family) extend to a stratification over an open of Spec Z? He expects it not to for a family with infinite monodromy. This predates Katz's 1972 statement and gives documentary prehistory of the conjecture, tied to modular curves and Hasse invariants.
missed.quote: nous venons de voir (ou presque ...) que cette stratification ne s'étend pas en une stratification sur S_U , U un ouvert non vide de Spec(Z)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit and dating of the p-curvature conjecture; links it explicitly to crystals and ordinary/supersingular phenomena.

missed.claim: Explicit 1966 analogy 'module with stratification ≈ ℓ-adic sheaf, sharing its rigidity', predating Gieseker's 1975 programme on stratified bundles and the conjectures later proved by Esnault–Mehta.
missed.quote: pour nous le module à stratification doit jouer dans une large mesure le rôle d'un faisceau ℓ-adique, dont il partage également les propriétés de rigidité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Attribution: the stratified-bundle / étale-local-system analogy is usually credited to Gieseker; here it appears in Grothendieck's 1966 Tate letter.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly exploratory and partly wrong reasoning, later superseded by Katz's p-curvature computation and Serre–Tate theory. The interest is historical: early appearances of the p-curvature-conjecture question and of the stratified-bundle/ℓ-adic analogy in 1966, plausibly underdocumented.
transcription_corrections: 'canularesque' is split across lines in the typescript as 'canulares-que'; the reading is correct.
The insertion reads 'pour nous le module à stratification': 'la' is corrected to 'le' with 'module à' added above.
The handwritten 's/' above 'schéma' in the first line makes it 'schémas modulaire'; the whole first paragraph is struck through by a diagonal line.
'S_U , U un ouvert': the U subscript was corrected by hand; the reading S_U is right.
